extracted.name: Easy Filipino Pandesal Recipe
extracted.description: Soft, fluffy, and slightly sweet, Easy Filipino Pandesal is a beloved traditional bread roll perfect for breakfast or merienda. These golden brown buns are coated in fine breadcrumbs and baked until lightly crisp on the outside, while the inside stays warm, pillowy, and tender. Made with simple ingredients like flour, yeast, sugar, and milk, this easy version simplifies the process without sacrificing the classic taste. Best enjoyed fresh from the oven with butter, cheese, or your favorite spread, pandesal is a comforting staple in every Filipino home.
ingredient_lines: 4 cups all-purpose flour (plus more for kneading)
1/4 cup unsalted butter, melted and slightly cooled
instruction_lines: In a small bowl, combine warm milk, 1 tbsp of the sugar, and yeast. Stir gently and let sit for 5–10 minutes, until foamy. In a large mixing bowl, combine flour, remaining sugar, and salt. Add the foamy yeast mixture, melted butter, and egg. Mix until a sticky dough forms.

Turn the dough onto a floured surface. Knead for 8–10 minutes, until soft, smooth, and elastic. (You can also use a stand mixer with a dough hook.) Place dough in a lightly greased bowl. Cover with a clean towel or plastic wrap. Let rise in a warm place for 1 to 1.5 hours, or until doubled in size.

Punch down the dough to release air. Divide dough into 20–24 equal portions (about golf ball size). Shape each piece into a smooth ball. Roll each ball lightly in breadcrumbs and place on a parchment-lined baking tray, spaced about 1 inch apart. Cover shaped rolls with a towel. Let rise again for 30–40 minutes, until puffy.

Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C). Bake rolls for 15–18 minutes, or until lightly golden on top. Let pandesal cool slightly on a wire rack. Serve warm with butter, cheese, jam, or your favorite fillings like corned beef, eggs, or peanut butter.

✅ Tips for Perfect Pandesal: Use bread flour instead of all-purpose for chewier texture (optional).Store leftovers in an airtight container and reheat in the oven for 5 minutes to revive fluffiness. Freeze shaped dough balls for later use — thaw, rise, and bake as needed.
